rows.subtopic: Mob and crowd behaviour (stampede, riot, online pile-on)
rows.description: An observer sees a rumour, often on messaging apps, turn a crowd angry at an innocent person. Verified facts arrive late while the outrage is already in motion.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtopic: Mob and crowd behaviour (stampede, riot, online pile-on)
rows.description: A friend messages the target privately, helps them stop reading comments and, if needed, reports abuse. Steady human contact matters more than public defence.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A young child announces who did what, mostly to get adult approval or to test rules. It is closer to reporting than malice, but it shows they already sense information is social currency.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child shares another's secret to feel special and closer to a friend. Passing on private news feels like a gift of trust, without seeing the betrayal to the one it concerns.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager talks about a peer's crush or mistake to bond with the group and gain status. The pleasure is real, and so is the nervous thought that they might be the next topic.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager learns that a false story about them is spreading. They feel hot shame, fear of every glance and a wish to disappear, and often cannot tell who started it.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager says I did not hear that, or changes the subject, when a rumour is offered. Stopping the chain costs a little popularity but builds a reputation as safe to confide in.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A student is told something unflattering about a friend. They feel curiosity and loyalty pulling in different directions, and choosing to check with the friend keeps trust intact.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: Some talk about others carries useful information, such as which professor is fair or which person is unreliable. The line between useful caution and cruel entertainment is intent and accuracy.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A young professional sees news travel through the pantry and messaging groups before official announcements. Those with good grapevine access feel powerful, and those outside feel anxious.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22
